> **Migrated from the `llm` worklog:** this item was originally filed there as `LP-0MVF4OPC1001RYX6` (deleted after migration on 2026-10-20). The `llm` repo remains the sweep target for its markers listed below; all skill-code changes live here in `SorraAgents`.

# Remove stale REFACTOR markers when their work item closes

## Problem statement

The refactor skill injects `REFACTOR-<id>` marker comments into source files to suppress duplicate work-item creation, but there is no removal path: once the referenced smell is fixed (or judged a false positive) and its work item closes, the marker persists and — because `has_existing_comment(file_path, smell_type)` matches on *smell type* only — permanently suppresses detection of that smell type in that file.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `/skill:refactor` or the implement pipeline's refactor step — they trust duplicate suppression to be accurate; a stale marker silently hides a real regression.
- **Developers reading source files** — stale markers are noise that misrepresents outstanding work.
- **Producers triaging the Refactor backlog** — a closed work item should leave no trace in the codebase.

Example user stories:

- "As an agent running the refactor step, when a marker's work item is already closed, I want the marker gone (or ignored) so I do not skip a smell that has regressed."
- "As a developer, when a refactor item is completed or judged a false positive, I want its comment removed from the file without touching surrounding code or line endings."
- "As a producer, I want a single command that reports every stale marker in the project and can clean them up."

## Existing state

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` provides `inject_refactor_comment()`, `has_existing_comment()`, `get_comment_style()` and `_build_comment_block()`; there is **no removal function**.
- Two slightly different regexes parse markers: `comment_injection.REFACTOR_PATTERN` (`REFACTOR-(\S+).*?smell:\s*(\S+)`, DOTALL) and `workitem_creation.REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN` (multi-line, expects a comment prefix before `smell:`).
- Markers are written in two shapes: line-prefixed (`# <!-- REFACTOR-…` … `# -->` for Python/YAML/shell, `// <!-- …` for JS/TS) and native block (`<!-- … -->` for Markdown/HTML). CSS-family files use `/* … */` with ` * ` prefixes.
- `inject_refactor_comment()` reads and writes text mode without `newline=""`, so injected files are normalised; removal must not repeat that mistake.
- `StatusLifecycle.show()` and `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags()` already provide safe work-item lookup and prefix-to-sibling worklog-store resolution. Verified: a bare `wl show <foreign-prefix-id>` fails ("Work item not found"), so a sweep **must** inject `--worklog-dir` from the shared resolver.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` `remediate_pre_existing()` injects markers only for smells it just filed items for; the pipeline syncs the worklog first (`wl sync --if-idle`) and has no post-close hook.
- The canonical source of the skill is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/` (symlinked into `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor`); its tests live in `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/`, with `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` (1251 lines) covering the current API.
- Stale markers confirmed at HEAD in the `llm` repo (work-item state checked 2026-10-20):

| File | Marker | Item stage |
|---|---|---|
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` | open / `intake_complete` — reported false positive |
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:8` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTV87EC4006EU5Z` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTRWI65I005VXOC` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/provider.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MSI4ZIF60064EOR` | completed / `done` |

- The same defect is visible in the `SorraAgents` repo itself: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (2 markers), `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` (3), `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (2), `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_regressions.py` — 4 of these reference `completed` items, the rest reference `open / idea` items.

## Desired change

1. **Removal API** in `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`: `remove_refactor_marker(file_path, work_item_id) -> dict` (or a small dataclass) that locates the whole marker block for that id — line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes — and deletes it, leaving the remainder of the file byte-identical (including CRLF/LF and the file's original trailing newline). Absent marker → `{"removed": False, "reason": "absent"}`; repeated runs are no-ops.
2. **Sweep module** (new `skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py`): discover markers in repo-tracked files (exclude `.worklog/`, `node_modules`, binaries), group by referenced work-item id to one `wl show` per distinct id (worklog dir resolved via `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags`), classify each marker as `stale` (stage `in_review`/`done`/`completed` or status `completed`), `active` (any other resolved stage) or `unknown` (lookup failed), and return a structured report.
3. **Trigger** from the refactor pipeline: run the sweep after the `wl sync` and **before** smell detection, so `has_existing_comment` never observes a stale marker. Non-fatal on `wl` failure (log a warning, keep markers). Standalone CLI entry point (`--sweep-markers`, report-only by default, `--apply` to delete) and a skip flag (`--no-marker-sweep`).
4. **`has_existing_comment` correctness**: keep it a pure file predicate by default, but accept an optional `is_active` resolver/callback so a caller can exclude terminal items; the pipeline's sweep-before-detect ordering is what makes the default path correct. `unknown` markers keep suppressing (conservative) and are reported as warnings.
5. **False-positive path**: a marker whose item is still open but was judged a false positive must be removable explicitly (`--remove-marker <work-item-id>` or `remove_refactor_marker()` called directly), independent of item stage.
6. **Unit tests** in `tests/test_refactor/`: removal for `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes; block and line-prefix styles; CRLF preservation; absent-marker no-op; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file touching only the target block; classification of `in_review`/`done`/`completed`/`open`; `unknown` id kept and reported; dry-run performs no writes; cross-store id resolution.
7. **Sweep the existing stale markers** in `llm` (6 stale; the false positive needs an explicit decision) and in `SorraAgents` (4 stale), so `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` afterwards shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
8. **Documentation**: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (§ REFACTOR Comments + flags table + report keys), `docs/refactor.md` (§ 4 Work Item Creation, troubleshooting "Duplicate work items created", module reference), and module docstrings. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (ship pipeline owns it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `remove_refactor_marker()` removes a `REFACTOR-<id>` marker block (line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles) from a file while leaving all surrounding content byte-identical and preserving the file's line endings (verified by a CRLF fixture test).
- [ ] Removal is a no-op (`removed=False`) when the marker is absent, and re-running it is idempotent.
- [ ] A sweep reports every marker in the project with its referenced item's stage and a classification of `stale` / `active` / `unknown`; removal is triggered for markers whose work item is at a terminal stage (`in_review`, `done`, `completed`).
- [ ] Sweep work-item lookups resolve the correct worklog store via the shared resolver (a foreign-prefix id resolves; failure is non-fatal and keeps the marker as `unknown`).
- [ ] `has_existing_comment()` no longer suppresses detection for closed work items — covered by a test asserting a terminal-stage marker is not treated as an existing comment on the sweep-before-detect path (and via the optional active-item filter).
- [ ] An explicit false-positive removal path exists for markers whose work item is still open, with `--dry-run` making no writes.
- [ ] Running the sweep (apply mode) removes the 6 stale `llm` markers listed above and the 4 stale `SorraAgents` markers; a follow-up `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles; absent marker; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file; terminal vs non-terminal classification; unknown id; dry-run no-write.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Canonical source is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/`; never edit `~/.pi/agent/skills/...` (the installer replaces it) and never hand-edit markers in `llm` outside an authorised implementation run.
- Standard library only — no new third-party dependencies.
- One `wl show` per distinct referenced work-item id (cached per run); the sweep must stay in the same sub-second-to-low-seconds envelope as the existing pipeline rather than spawning per marker.
- Sweep is read-only unless `--apply` (or the default pipeline policy) removes stale markers; `--dry-run` must never write.
- Never remove a marker for an item that is not terminal unless explicitly requested by id.
- Only scan git-tracked files in the repo root (skip `.worklog/`, worktrees, `node_modules`, binary files).
- Work-item ids may belong to sibling project stores; always route `wl` through the shared resolver, not the cwd default.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — add `remove_refactor_marker()`, a single tolerant marker parser covering both existing regexes, `is_active` filter hook on `has_existing_comment()`, and `newline=""` IO.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py` (new) — marker discovery, per-id work-item lookup via `shared.status_lifecycle`, classification and report structure.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — sweep step after `wl sync` / before detection, `--sweep-markers`, `--apply`, `--remove-marker`, `--no-marker-sweep` flags, report keys.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — reuse the unified marker pattern instead of its own `REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN`.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — marker lifecycle and new flags.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/docs/refactor.md` — § 4, troubleshooting, module reference.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — extend with removal tests.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_marker_sweep.py` (new) — sweep classification, dry-run, unknown ids, non-fatal wl failures.
- `llm`: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py`, `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — sweep targets only (no hand edits).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Repository placement (assumption A1):** the skill's source of truth is `SorraAgents`, so the code change belongs here (this `SA-` item) and owns the `llm` marker sweep alongside the `SorraAgents` sweep; Q1 is resolved by this migration.
- **No close hook:** `wl` exposes no plugin/hook on close (only `wl plugins` for discovery), so "triggered when the item reaches a terminal stage" is implemented as a sweep at refactor-run time plus a standalone command — not an event. Assumption A2.
- **False-positive regression loop:** removing the marker for a closed false-positive item re-enables detection, so the next scan re-files the same item. Mitigation: false positives must be closed with a reason *and* either fixed or excluded via `.refactor.json`/per-file ignore; the sweep should report (not silently hide) this case. Scope-creep risk — an ignore-list mechanism is a separate work item.
- **Mixed answers to `unknown`:** unresolvable ids (deleted items, wrong store) could hide real work. Conservative default: keep + warn.
- **Formatting churn:** a naive implementation strips a leading blank line or rewrites CRLF files, producing whole-file diffs. Byte-preserving IO (`newline=""`, explicit trailing-newline handling) plus a CRLF fixture test is mandatory.
- **Regex divergence:** the two existing patterns disagree on block styles; unifying them is required or Markdown/CSS markers will be missed by the sweep.
- **Scope creep:** generalising to a lifecycle framework for all agent-injected comments is out of scope; record as a separate item if it surfaces.

## Open questions

1. **Repository and work-item placement** — ~~implement in `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor` under a new `SA-` item (this `LP-` item keeps the `llm` sweep and records the blocker), or keep everything under this `LP-` item and treat the SorraAgents edits as out-of-worktree?~~ **RESOLVED** by migration: this `SA-` item hosts the skill change; the `llm` marker list below stays the sweep target.
2. **Trigger surface** — sweep automatically inside the refactor pipeline (default) plus a standalone `--sweep-markers --apply`, or standalone-only (manual/cron)?
3. **False positives and unresolvable ids** — should `has_existing_comment` keep suppressing on `unknown` ids (conservative) while a manual `--remove-marker <id>` handles false positives, or should both be dropped automatically?

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which repository should host the skill change — `SorraAgents/skill/refactor` (canonical source, its own `SA-` item) or this `LP-` item in `llm`? (moot — item migrated to `SorraAgents` as `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9`)" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor`; the skill's tests live in `SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/`; `implement.py` creates worktrees from the cwd's `.worklog`, so an `LP-` item cannot legally host edits under `SorraAgents`. **Recommended:** new `SA-` item in `SorraAgents` for the skill change, `SA-0MVGQHKI8003HWO9` scoped to the `llm` marker sweep and recording the blocker.
- Q: "How should the terminal-stage trigger be implemented, given `wl` exposes no close hook?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: `wl plugins` only lists plugins; no event/hook surface found; the refactor pipeline already runs at the end of implementation and syncs first. **Recommended:** sweep inside the refactor pipeline (after `wl sync`, before detection) plus a standalone `--sweep-markers` report/`--apply` CLI.
- Q: "Should markers referencing unresolvable work items, and false-positive markers whose item is still open, be removed automatically?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: all `llm` markers resolve today except none; `LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` is open at `intake_complete` while the marker is documented as a false positive. **Recommended:** keep `unknown` markers and warn; require an explicit `--remove-marker <id>` for open-item false positives.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE** – Refactor: Formatting in a test file of the (since-deleted) `proxy-usage-analysis` skill (open)
- **LP-0MQ5NI704006WINH** – Unit tests: cooldown behavior (completed)
- **LP-0MROYEVL3004Y04Z** – Manually fix remaining 5 non-auto-fixable lint errors (4 F401, 1 F811) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts.txt` — matched: absent, accept, acceptance, accurate, active (+400 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_nothink.txt` — matched: absent, accept, acceptance, accurate, active (+400 more)
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts_think.txt` — matched: absent, accept, acceptance, accurate, active (+400 more)

data.description:
# Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6)

## Problem statement

Implement sessions that run concurrently spend the overwhelming majority of their
wall-clock waiting on a single per-repository `flock`, because `implement.py finish`
holds that lock across its **whole** commit → fast-forward → push → post-push window
and the dev-push **pre-push hook runs the full test suite (~5.4 min)** inside it.
Every concurrent `finish` therefore serialises its expensive test run behind the
others. At the intended fan-out of **up to 6 concurrent sessions**, the sixth finish
queues behind five ~5-min full-suite runs.

## Evidence (2026-11-13, AI_Hell implement-skill sessions)

Analysed the 36 worktree sessions that started with the implement skill
(`~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell-.worklog-*`):

- **668 min** summed session time over a **388 min (6.5 h)** wall-clock span —
  only **1.7x effective parallelism** at a **peak measured concurrency of 4**.
- **88–93%** of each long session's wall-clock was inside `bash` tool calls
  (waiting on processes), not model reasoning or edits.
- Time buckets: **wait_for_job 249 min (37%)** (215.9 min of it lock-waits),
  own `finish` 133 min (20%), scoped tests 57 min (9%), hand-rolled
  `sleep`/`grep` polling loops 48 min (7%).
- **57** "another run holds the repository lock" refusals; **46** observed
  lock-waits averaging **4.3 min** (median 5 min, **max 21.5 min**). Worst single
  tool call: **45 min** = a `for attempt in 1..8` retry loop absorbing five
  consecutive lock holders.
- **21** non-fast-forward rebase events, each creating a new tree that re-triggers
  the full-suite pre-push gate (9 full-suite gate runs today).
- 9 sessions were **no-ops** (3 messages, ~50 s) — drive retries that immediately
  gave up.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions
  (the intended operating point) on a single repository.
- **Implement-skill sessions** (leaf and driven child) whose `finish` currently queues
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs.
- **Producers/reviewers** who need the speed-up evidenced, not asserted.

User stories:

- As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
  complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised queueing
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in roughly the
  time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.
- As a driven child session, I want my single `finish` call to wait boundedly on the
  lock instead of scripting retry loops.
- As a producer, I want a recorded before/after measurement before the epic is closed.

## Goal

As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised
queueing behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in
roughly the time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.

## Decomposition

The epic is decomposed into five child items; together they own every acceptance
criterion below.

1. Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock
   (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — the single biggest time sink: stop holding the exclusive
   repository lock across the ~5.4 min full-suite gate.
2. Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops
   (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF) — replace fail-fast refusals plus agent-scripted retry loops
   with one bounded internal wait that reports the holder.
3. Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC) — a lost
   push race currently pays the full suite again because the rebase produces a new tree.
4. Eliminate no-op drive retries that spawn and immediately give up
   (SA-0MWFJSCPT005BO2R) — 9 of 36 sessions did no work.
5. Measure the 6-way concurrent finish fan-out and record before/after analysis
   (SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E) — verifies the outcome ACs against real session logs; blocked
   by items 1–4.

## Acceptance criteria

- Under a 6-way concurrent `finish` fan-out, no session spends the majority of its
  wall-clock blocked on the per-repository lock (measured: median lock-wait per session < 60 s; no single lock-wait > 5 min).
- The full test suite is never executed while a single global repository lock is held (proved by inspection + test).
- A waiting `finish` performs **one** bounded internal wait rather than N fail-fast round-trips, and the skill guidance contains no bespoke `for attempt ...; wait_for_job` finish retry loops.
- A concrete before/after measurement is recorded (same 36-session style analysis).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Safety invariants stay intact: single-owner mutation of the shared `dev` ref, the
  bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and tree/provenance binding of gate verdicts
  (no verdict about a different tree/diff may be trusted).
- The dev-push gate keeps `scope=full` for release-critical refs — the speed-up must not
  weaken the release gate.
- Target concurrency is **up to 6**; designs are evaluated at that fan-out.

## Existing state

- `implement.py finish` acquires `<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock`
  (`shared.repo_lock.RepoLock`) at Step 3c and holds it through push and post-push
  verification; `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` defaults to 0 (fail fast).
- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --gate-commit <sha>` for
  pushes to `dev`/`main`, with a tree-keyed verdict cache (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`)
  and gate provenance lines, all of which execute inside the held finish lock today.
- Pushes to the shared `dev` ref lose the non-fast-forward race under concurrency; the
  rebase-and-retry path in `implement.py` produces a new tree and therefore a cache miss.
- `phase_drive` spawns one session per child; some spawns observe state that makes the
  child immediately terminal/blocked and exit as no-ops.

## Desired change

Concurrent `finish` runs overlap their expensive work instead of serialising on one
repository-wide critical section, and the epic's outcome is evidenced by a recorded
before/after session analysis.

## Impact

An operator can run a 6-way concurrent implement fan-out and have the batch finish in
roughly the time of one work item, instead of waiting for six serialised five-minute
test runs — while still shipping only fully tested commits.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 3c lock window, push/rebase retry path, `phase_drive` spawn decisions
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `RepoLock` / bounded wait for `main-checkout.lock`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — full-suite gate, `test` semaphore lane, tree-keyed verdict cache
- `.githooks/pre-push` — dev/main full-suite gate and cache mirroring
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish/wait guidance to update
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_lock_timeout_isolation.py`, `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — existing regression coverage to extend

## Related work

- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — the lock/wait helper this epic shrinks the critical section of.
- implement.py finish: concurrent sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev fast-forward (SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY) — established the single-owner lock invariant.
- Hermetic regression tests for finish concurrency orphans (SA-0MVPZG01J0067PC2) — concurrency test patterns to reuse.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the full suite sits at the gate.
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache that makes verdict reuse possible.
- Session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — this epic's measurement items should reuse/feed it.
- Post-fix slot-wait re-measurement (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K) — precedent methodology for before/after measurement.
- Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs (SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5) — push-race prior art.

## Out of scope

- Trimming the full suite's own runtime / sharding / per-file caching, and raising
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` — those are per-project (AI_Hell) concerns, not framework.
- Changing changed-scope test selection.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** moving the suite out of the lock could let an untested tree reach `dev`;
  mitigation is the tree/provenance-bound verdict and the ancestry assertion, both
  preserved by the owning children.
- **Risk:** verdict reuse after a rebase could accept a genuinely different diff;
  mitigated by provable content equality plus a negative test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** building a general lock/push queue service is out of scope;
  the children take the smallest change that meets their ACs.
- **Assumption:** the measured symptom is lock serialisation, not per-project suite
  runtime — the baseline bucket analysis supports this (37% in `wait_for_job`, 215.9 min
  of it lock-waits).
- **Assumption:** sessions of comparable work-item size are available for the "after"
  measurement; otherwise a synthetic 6-way fan-out supplies it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What concurrency target must the design satisfy?" — Answer (operator, 2026-11-13):
  "Up to 6 concurrent implement sessions." Source: analysis comment on this item
  (SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR).
- Q: "Is trimming the per-project full test suite runtime in scope?" — Answer (operator,
  2026-11-13): "No — per-project (AI_Hell) suite trimming, sharding and
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` changes are out of scope for this epic." Source: same comment.
- Q: "What is the evidence base for the problem statement?" — Answer: the 2026-11-13
  AI_Hell analysis of 36 implement-skill sessions (668 min summed over a 388 min span;
  1.7x effective parallelism; 46 lock-waits, median 5 min, max 21.5 min; 21 rebases;
  9 no-op sessions). Source: comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR and the "Evidence" section
  above.
- Q: "Does the epic already own a measurement/verification item?" — Answer (this intake,
  research: `wl list --parent SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1`): no — the four original children all
  change code, so the outcome ACs had no owner; child 5
  (SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E) was created to own them.

### Plan session (2026-11-13)

- Q: "Are further clarifying questions needed before the decomposition is final?"
  Answer (agent, research: full re-read of all five children plus repository verification
  of `implement.py` Step 3c / `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `.githooks/pre-push`,
  `run_tests.py` tree-keyed cache and `phase_drive`): no — the four intake answers
  (concurrency target 6; per-project suite trimming out of scope; evidence base;
  measurement ownership) already fix scope, and every child's factual claims check out
  against the current code.
- Q: "Does each root cause need a separate test-only work item before implementation?"
  Answer (agent, applying the plan skill's vertical-slice rule): no — every child carries

# Set assignee per skill

## Problem statement

Skills currently claim work items using the producer identity (`Map`) as the assignee. This makes an agent's claim indistinguishable from a producer hold and prevents the claim reaper from identifying which skill is actually working. Each skill should instead claim with its own name.

## Users

- **Producers** — need to identify which skill is actively working on a work item from the assignee field.
- **Automated systems** (downtime dispatcher, claim reaper) — need accurate assignee attribution to detect and release stale claims.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Intake skill** — `intake.py start` defaults to `assignee="Intake"` when no explicit assignee is passed; callers that hard-code `--assignee Map` are updated to either omit the flag (using the new default) or use `--assignee Intake`.
2. **Plan skill** — any explicit `--assignee Map` claim in the plan skill's documentation is updated to `--assignee Plan` (or removed if the skill already claims without an assignee).
3. **Implement skill** — any explicit `--assignee Map` claim is updated to `--assignee Implement` (or removed if the skill already claims without an assignee).
4. **Audit skill** — any explicit `--assignee Map` claim is updated to `--assignee Audit` (or removed if already using `--assignee ""`).
5. **All other skill documentation** — any remaining references to `--assignee Map` in SKILL.md files are updated to use the appropriate skill name.
6. **Assignee release unchanged** — the assignee-clearing behaviour on every terminal outcome (finish, auto-complete, abort, error) is preserved exactly as-is.

## Impact

Producers and automated systems can now distinguish which skill is actively working on a work item by inspecting the assignee field, and the claim reaper can reliably identify and release stale skill-level claims.

## Constraints

- Only the *claim* assignee changes; release-by-default on every terminal outcome is unaffected.
- The `PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT` constant and the `claim_release.py` shared module must continue to treat `Map` as a claimable identity — no changes to shared infrastructure.
- No new work items should be created during the change; only existing skill documentation and any skill scripts that hard-code `Map` are modified.

## Existing state

- The intake skill instructs agents to pass `--assignee Map` to `intake.py start`.
- The `claim_release.py` module defines `PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT = "Map"` and treats it as a normal claim (released on terminal outcomes).
- The plan skill already claims without an assignee (`StatusLifecycle.update_status(work_item_id, "in_progress")` with no assignee kwarg).
- The implement skill also claims without an assignee (`StatusLifecycle.update_status(work_item_id, "in_progress")` with no assignee kwarg).

## Desired change

Replace `--assignee Map` with the skill's own name (e.g., `--assignee Intake`, `--assignee Audit`) in skill documentation and any scripts that hard-code this pattern, so each skill's claim is self-attributing.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/intake/SKILL.md` — Update `--assignee Map` references to `--assignee Intake`.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/intake/scripts/intake.py` — Change default assignee in `cmd_start` from None to `"Intake"`.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/SKILL.md` — Check for any `--assignee Map` references; update if present.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/plan/SKILL.md` — Verify claim pattern; update if needed.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Verify claim pattern; update if needed.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared/claim_release.py` — No changes required (Map remains a valid claimable identity).

## Related work

- SA-0MW7QTAHW0030FGV — Planned items are still left with an assignee (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6GWG005VIFK — T1: Table-driven assignee-release regression matrix (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6OJY000JZBL — Flip StatusLifecycle assignee-release default (completed)
- SA-0MVVF6Y38004T5OZ — Migrate callers and pin intentional holds (completed)
- SA-0MVR929TS000C8UM — implement/intake: clear assignee on completion regardless of outcome (completed)

No questions asked — the task scope is clear from the work-item description.
